question:
A small remote office is set to connect to the regional hub site via NSSA ASBR.
Which type of LSA is sent to the remote office OSPF area?
explanation: The remote site is connected to the Hub site via an ASBR router. Hence, an ASBR router redistributes a non OSPF or an External route into the NSSA area which is a Type 7. There is no ABR router in the question.
theory: A Not-So-Stubby Area (NSSA) behaves like a stub area (no external Type 5 LSAs allowed in) but still permits an ASBR inside the NSSA to redistribute external routes. That ASBR generates Type 7 (NSSA External) LSAs, which flood only within the NSSA; an ABR bordering the backbone may optionally translate them to Type 5 for the rest of the domain. Since the remote office connects via an NSSA ASBR (not an ABR), the LSA it receives for the redistributed route is Type 7. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 1 — OSPF NSSA)
